title: ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger
exclusions: Excludes generic IT-network anomalies that do not touch the SIS zone or its conduits (those are covered by IT-side CIM / network UCs). Excludes routine BPCS-only events that do not cross into the SIS zone.
evidence: Saved search `UC-22.63.6` archived hourly to `audit_evidence` with `iec_clause="ISA-TR84-00-09-s4"`. Every SIS-relevant cyber-event pins (event_id, sis_id, zone_id, conduit_id, event_type, mitre_ot_technique_id, severity, cra_finding_link_ref, pha_trigger_status, risk_score).

compliance.assurance_rationale: ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 (Integrated cybersecurity programme) requires that cybersecurity events affecting the SIS or its conduits feed back into the SIS Cybersecurity Risk Assessment and, if the events suggest a new hazard scenario, into the Process Hazard Analysis (PHA). This UC enforces both feed-back loops: every SIS-zone or SIS-conduit security event creates a linked CRA finding (UC-22.63.2) and, on threshold-exceedance, triggers a PHA refresh request (UC-22.63.5 MoC pipeline).
compliance.controlObjective: Demonstrates that the integrated cybersecurity programme detects SIS-relevant cyber-events and feeds them back into the CRA and PHA processes.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search archived to `audit_evidence`, the `Integrated SIS Cybersecurity Programme` dashboard, the cross-linked CRA finding register, the PHA-refresh request log.

compliance.assurance_rationale: ISA-TR84.00.09 §5 (Cybersecurity risk assessment methodology) provides the methodology for the CRA. The feed-back UC partially supports §5 by ensuring the CRA is driven by real field-events rather than only by design-time assumptions. Full §5 compliance also requires the structured CRA methodology — that limb is enforced by UC-22.63.2.
compliance.controlObjective: Provides the field-event-feed-back limb of §5 CRA methodology.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-22.63.6 positive (ISA, TR84.00.09, integrated, cybersecurity, programme:): ingest synthetic events into `index=ot_sis` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `detected_at` grouped by `event_id` satisfies `ack_lag_min` > 30, or `risk_score` > 0 for 'ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-22.63.6 negative (refresh trigger): ingest benign `ot_sis` / `target_sourcetype` events where `event_id` stays below `ack_lag_min` > 30, or `risk_score` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv`. Variant 9 confirms zero alert rows for 'ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger'.

dataSources: Splunk OT Security Add-on events tagged with SIS-zone or SIS-conduit IDs. SIS logic-solver anomaly events. KV Store `iec_61511_sis_zone_conduit_lookup` (zone_id, conduit_id, sis_id, sl_target, sl_capability, sl_achieved). KV Store `iec_61511_sis_relevant_cyber_event_register_lookup` (event_id, sis_id, event_type, severity, mitre_ot_technique_id, cra_finding_link_ref, pha_trigger_status, sla_acknowledged_at, sla_cra_linked_at, sla_pha_decided_at).
app: Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk OT Security Add-on (Splunkbase 6849).
spl:
index=ot_sis OR index=ot_security sis_relevance="true" earliest=-24h@h
| eval mitre_ot_technique_id = coalesce(mitre_ot_technique_id, mitre_attack_ics_technique)
| eval severity = coalesce(severity, alert_severity)
| stats values(mitre_ot_technique_id) as mitre_ot_technique_id, max(_time) as detected_at, latest(severity) as severity, latest(zone_id) as zone_id, latest(conduit_id) as conduit_id, latest(sis_id) as sis_id by event_id
| join type=left event_id [
    | inputlookup iec_61511_sis_relevant_cyber_event_register_lookup
    | table event_id cra_finding_link_ref pha_trigger_status sla_acknowledged_at sla_cra_linked_at sla_pha_decided_at
  ]
| eval now_ts = now()
| eval ack_lag_min = round((sla_acknowledged_at - detected_at) / 60, 1)
| eval cra_lag_hours = round((sla_cra_linked_at - detected_at) / 3600, 1)
| eval pha_lag_hours = round((sla_pha_decided_at - detected_at) / 3600, 1)
| eval no_ack = if(isnull(sla_acknowledged_at) AND (now_ts - detected_at) > 300, 1, 0)
| eval no_cra_link = if(isnull(sla_cra_linked_at) AND (now_ts - detected_at) > 28800, 1, 0)
| eval pha_undecided = if(isnull(sla_pha_decided_at) AND severity IN ("critical","high") AND (now_ts - detected_at) > 86400, 1, 0)
| eval risk_score = case(
    no_ack = 1, 100,
    no_cra_link = 1 AND severity IN ("critical","high"), 100,
    no_cra_link = 1, 95,
    pha_undecided = 1, 90,
    sla_pha_decided_at > sla_cra_linked_at + 86400, 70,
    ack_lag_min > 30 AND severity IN ("critical","high"), 60,
    1=1, 0)
| where risk_score > 0
| sort 0 -risk_score, +ack_lag_min
| table event_id sis_id zone_id conduit_id severity mitre_ot_technique_id detected_at ack_lag_min cra_lag_hours pha_lag_hours risk_score
description: Detects UC-22.63.6 — ISA, TR84.00.09, integrated, cybersecurity, programme: — using `index=ot_sis` sourcetype `configured sourcetype`, grouped by `event_id`. Outputs `detected_at` each `the scheduled window`; alert when `ack_lag_min` > 30, or `risk_score` > 0. Primary focus: refresh trigger. Purpose-built for 'ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger' in Compliance workflows.
value: Operators running UC-22.63.6 on UC-22.63.6 search results shorten triage for refresh trigger tied to 'ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger', lowering audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays.
implementation: (1) Tag every Splunk OT Security event with `sis_relevance = true / false` via a `transforms.conf` lookup against `iec_61511_sis_zone_conduit_lookup`. (2) Maintain `iec_61511_sis_relevant_cyber_event_register_lookup` with the SLA timestamps captured as the FSM-cyber team works the event. (3) Schedule UC-22.63.6 hourly; route `risk_score = 100` to the on-call FSM-cyber team + Functional Safety Manager at severity P1 (paging).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised IEC 61511 control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'ISA-TR84.00.09 §4 integrated cybersecurity programme: SIS-relevant security-incident detection feed-back into Cybersecurity Risk Assessment register and Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) refresh trigger' (UC-22.63.6) on `event_id` during scheduled clause ISA-TR84-00-09-s4 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=ot_sis` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `ack_lag_min` > 30. Cross-check engagement letter in `iec_61511_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `ot_sis` for `event_id`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `event_id` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `iec_61511_exception_register.csv` keyed on `event_id`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
equipmentModels: Claroty xDome / Dragos Platform / Nozomi Guardian / Tenable.ot (OT detection sources)
reviewer: Functional Safety Manager + CISO + Process Safety Manager + Board Safety Committee
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

- UC-22.63.2 (CRA register) and UC-22.63.5 (MoC register) deployed.
- An OT-detection capability (Claroty / Dragos / Nozomi / Tenable.ot) sending events to Splunk with SIS-zone tagging.
- A nominated FSM-cyber on-call rota.

## Step 1 - Zone-and-conduit lookup

```ini
[iec_61511_sis_zone_conduit_lookup]
enforceTypes = true
field.zone_id = string
field.conduit_id = string
field.sis_id = string
field.sl_target = string
field.sl_capability = string
field.sl_achieved = string
```

## Step 2 - SIS-relevant-cyber-event register

```ini
[iec_61511_sis_relevant_cyber_event_register_lookup]
enforceTypes = true
field.event_id = string
field.sis_id = string
field.event_type = string
field.severity = string
field.mitre_ot_technique_id = string
field.cra_finding_link_ref = string
field.pha_trigger_status = string
field.sla_acknowledged_at = time
field.sla_cra_linked_at = time
field.sla_pha_decided_at = time
field.dismissal_basis_ref = string
field.expected_write_pattern_ref = string
field.tool_maintenance_window_ref = string
```

## Step 3 - SIS-relevance enrichment

At index-time enrichment:

```ini
[ot_sis_relevance]
LOOKUP-sis-relevance = iec_61511_sis_zone_conduit_lookup zone_id, conduit_id OUTPUT sis_id AS sis_id, sl_target AS sl_target
EVAL-sis_relevance = if(isnotnull(sis_id), "true", "false")
```

## Step 4 - Schedule

```ini
[UC-22.63.6: Integrated SIS Cybersecurity Programme]
cron_schedule = 13 * * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -24h@h
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index, notable
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.63.6,reg=IEC-61511,clause=ISA-TR84-00-09-s4
alert.severity = 5
```

## Step 5 - Functional-safety-specific notes

- **PHA-refresh decision criteria**: the FSM-cyber team should apply a documented decision-rubric (e.g., 'new failure-mode not in PHA' → PHA refresh; 'known failure-mode with previously-considered cyber-cause' → CRA update only).
- **Board reporting**: the SLA-conformance metric from this UC is typically the headline cyber-safety-bridge metric reported quarterly to the Board Safety Committee.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk OT Security Add-on (Splunkbase 6849).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into ot_sis, ot_security. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`ack_lag_min, event_id, no_ack, no_cra_link`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: When a cyber event touches a safety system, the safety team must be told right away, the cyber-risk record updated, and a decision made on whether to re-do the broader safety study. We watch every safety-touching cyber event and make sure all three of those happen on time.
